title: Correcting the Customer Without Winning an Argument
script: Laila: [warmly] Ms. Laila, your invoice charges us for delivery, but your salesperson promised free delivery.
Mr. Budi: Thank you for telling me. Do you have the quotation or message where that was stated?
Laila: [thoughtful] Yes, here is the email. It says delivery is included for orders above ten boxes.
Mr. Budi: I see that. Your order has eight boxes, so the automatic invoice added the normal fee.
Laila: [carefully] The salesperson knew we were ordering eight. He still told me there would be no charge.
Mr. Budi: Let me check the earlier message in the thread. Please give me a moment.
Laila: [reflective] Of course. I do not want to pay a fee that appeared after we agreed.
Mr. Budi: I found his message. You are correct: he specifically offered free delivery for this first order.
Laila: [honestly] Then the invoice should be changed.
Mr. Budi: Yes. I will remove the fee and send a corrected invoice today. I apologize for the inconsistency.
Laila: [gently] Thank you. I was worried you would only repeat the general policy.
Mr. Budi: The policy explains why the system added the fee, but it does not cancel a written promise made to you.
Laila: [encouraging] How will we avoid this on the next order?
Mr. Budi: I will add the standard threshold to your account note. Any exception must also appear clearly in the quotation before approval.
Laila: [sincere] That is fair. We may order more than ten boxes next time anyway.
Mr. Budi: I will also speak privately with the salesperson so special offers are entered into the billing system.
Laila: I appreciate that you checked the evidence instead of treating my complaint as an attack.
Mr. Budi: And I appreciate that you brought the email. The goal is an accurate invoice, not winning an argument.
Laila: Please send the correction to both me and our finance address.
Mr. Budi: I will. You should receive it within one hour, with the original invoice marked as canceled.

quiz.question: What fee does Mr. Budi question?
quiz.explanation: He expected delivery to be free.

quiz.question: What is the normal free-delivery rule?
quiz.explanation: The automated invoice followed a quantity threshold.

quiz.question: What evidence changes the result?
quiz.explanation: The email clearly offered an exception.

quiz.question: How will future exceptions be handled?
options: Written in quotations and billing records
quiz.explanation: Clear records align sales and billing.

quiz.question: What approach resolves the complaint?
options: Check evidence and correct the invoice without defensiveness
quiz.explanation: Accuracy is treated as the shared goal.

quiz.question: Why does the normal system add delivery?
options: The order has eight boxes, below the standard threshold
quiz.explanation: The rule explains the automated result.

quiz.question: What changes the correct outcome?
options: The next order may be larger
A written offer specifically promises free delivery for this order
quiz.explanation: Case-specific evidence overrides the general assumption.

quiz.question: Why is the policy still useful?
options: It proves the customer is wrong
It explains the system behavior even though it cannot cancel the exception
quiz.explanation: A cause and a contractual result can differ.

quiz.question: How will the company prevent repetition?
options: Record standard thresholds and approved exceptions in quotation and billing systems
Ask customers to remember every promise

quiz.question: What closes the correction clearly?
options: A new invoice is sent and the original is marked canceled
quiz.explanation: Document status prevents duplicate or uncertain payment.
